input: The pump that has been selected for this particular duty is a centrifugal unit, and its role is to move caustic solution between two vessels that are both situated at grade. At the specified duty point, the pump delivers a flow of 48 m3 h-1 against a head of 28 m, and it operates at this point with an efficiency of 71%, which can be regarded as a perfectly respectable figure for a service of this kind. The shaft power that is absorbed at the duty point amounts to some 5.2 kW, and the motor that drives the pump has been rated 15% above this value, so that a comfortable degree of margin is available to accommodate the kinds of variation that inevitably arise in normal operation. It is, moreover, reassuring to note that no evidence of cavitation was observed at any stage during the acceptance test, although it is only fair to point out that the test in question was run for a period of 4 h and, furthermore, that it was carried out at the duty point only. As a consequence, the behaviour of the pump under conditions that depart from the duty point has yet to be demonstrated, and some caution is therefore appropriate when it comes to extrapolating the test results to other operating regimes that the pump may encounter in service.
target: A centrifugal pump moves caustic solution between two vessels at grade. At the duty point the flow is 48 m3 h-1 against a head of 28 m, with a pump efficiency of 71%. Shaft power at the duty point is 5.2 kW, and the motor is rated 15% above this value. Cavitation was not observed in the acceptance test. The acceptance test ran for 4 h and at the duty point only, so its result is a statement about that operating point: the pump ran there without cavitation, at the flow and head the service specifies. The test states nothing about higher flows, where the suction condition tightens, or about sustained operation away from the point at which the efficiency is quoted. The margin the installation carries for duties above the specified point is the difference between the motor rating and the shaft power at the duty point, and any increase in the required flow or head moves the duty point and raises the shaft power against that fixed margin. The figures also fix what the pump costs to run at the specified duty, since the energy drawn in service follows from the shaft power and the hours spent at the point. A service that lives at its duty point is fully described by them. A service that moves around its duty point is described by them only at the point itself, and the acceptance test, confined as it is to that point, cannot be stretched to cover the rest of the operating range.
